styles.title: Rustic Barn Wedding Seating Layouts
styles.h1: How to Plan Seating for a Rustic Barn Wedding
styles.description: Discover how to arrange seating in a rustic barn venue. Focus on long wooden tables and open floor plans.

faqs.question: What are the best tables for a barn wedding?
faqs.answer: Long rectangular farmhouse tables are the most popular choice for barn weddings as they complement the rustic aesthetic and encourage communal dining.

faqs.question: How do I handle pillars in a barn?
faqs.answer: Use pillars as natural dividers between the dining area and the dance floor, and ensure tables are spaced at least 60 inches away from any structural supports.

styles.title: Ballroom Elegance: Formal Wedding Seating
styles.description: Master the art of formal seating in grand ballrooms with round tables and sophisticated layouts.

faqs.question: How many people fit at a standard ballroom table?
faqs.answer: Most ballrooms use 60-inch round tables which seat 8 guests comfortably, or 72-inch rounds which can accommodate 10 to 12 guests.

faqs.question: Where should the head table be placed in a ballroom?
faqs.answer: The head table should be the focal point, typically placed against a main wall or on a riser facing the dance floor and the rest of the guests.

guest-counts.title: Intimate Wedding Seating: 50 Guests
guest-counts.h1: Seating Chart Ideas for Intimate Weddings of 50 Guests
guest-counts.description: Small weddings offer unique seating opportunities. Explore layouts for 50 guests that feel cozy and connected.

faqs.question: What is the best layout for 50 guests?
faqs.answer: A U-shaped table or one long continuous table is excellent for 50 guests, as it allows everyone to see each other and feels like a large family dinner.

guest-counts.title: Seating Charts for 150 Guests
guest-counts.description: The 150-guest wedding is the most common size. Learn how to balance groups and ensure smooth flow.

faqs.question: How many tables do I need for 150 guests?
faqs.answer: For 150 guests, you will need approximately 19 tables of 8 guests each, or 15 tables of 10 guests each.

guest-counts.title: Large Wedding Seating: 300+ Guests
guest-counts.h1: Managing Seating for Large Receptions of 300 Guests
guest-counts.description: Scaling up to 300 guests requires precision. Learn how to avoid bottlenecks and manage large floor plans.

faqs.question: How do I manage a seating chart for 300 people?
faqs.answer: Use a digital tool to categorize guests into groups and ensure you have multiple large seating chart displays at the entrance to avoid crowding.

venue-types.title: Beach Wedding Seating & Layouts
venue-types.h1: Planning the Perfect Beach Wedding Seating Chart
venue-types.description: Seating guests on sand requires special considerations. Explore beach-friendly layouts and chair options.

faqs.question: Can I use standard chairs on a beach?
faqs.answer: Yes, but ensure you use chairs with wider legs or 'sand skids' to prevent them from sinking into the sand.

venue-types.title: Garden Party Wedding Seating Guide
venue-types.description: Leverage natural beauty with garden layouts that work with trees, paths, and floral borders.

faqs.question: How do I deal with uneven ground in a garden?
faqs.answer: Always visit the site and mark the flattest areas for table placement. Use shims if necessary to level table legs.

venue-types.title: Outdoor Tent Wedding Seating
venue-types.h1: How to Arrange Seating Under a Wedding Tent
venue-types.description: Tent poles and sidewalls change the dynamics of a floor plan. Learn how to optimize your tented reception.

faqs.question: Where should the bar go in a tent?
faqs.answer: Place the bar near the entrance or close to the dance floor, but away from the main dining tables to prevent overcrowding.
